The detection module itself (Faster R-CNN) is robust, with high precision and recall. The authors also isolate the contribution of the super-resolution component, showing a measurable 2% gain. Yet, the paper provides **zero** measurements of latency, memory, or power consumption. There is even no hardware specified for the "~20ms" super-resolution claim. A paper claiming a system is optimized for edge constraints while offering no constraints data effectively renders the primary architectural justification unfounded. This is not a minor omission; it is the central thesis of the work.
2.  **Lack of Decomposition:** The massive performance gap (32% relative improvement over Dynamsoft) is presented as a system result. There is no ablation showing how much of that gain comes from the novel detection (which is just Faster R-CNN, a standard model) versus the image preprocessing pipeline. Without showing that a vanilla decoder would fail significantly worse without the preprocessing, the claim that the *entire* pipeline is the breakthrough is weak.
